verdict.summary: Coherent Corp is the backbone of AI datacenter connectivity. The company manufactures optical transceivers, photonic components, and laser systems that move data inside and between hyperscale data centers. NVIDIA just committed $2B in investment plus multi-year purchase commitments for Coherent's next-gen optics — a de facto validation that optical interconnect is the bottleneck holding back AI scaling. With $6.3B TTM revenue growing at 17.5%, 73% earnings growth, and a Wyckoff markup phase in full swing from $88 to $299, the stock pulled back 21% from its March 4 high to $236.90. This dip offers a tactical entry into one of the strongest AI infrastructure plays on the market.

risks.pedagogy: The March 2-6 decline from $299 to $236 was caused by three factors: (1) profit-taking after a +240% rally from August lows, (2) broader market risk-off from Iran conflict escalation and oil spike, (3) high beta amplifying normal market moves. Critically, there was no negative company-specific news — in fact, the NVIDIA partnership was announced during the decline. This is a textbook macro-driven correction in a stock with strong fundamentals.

tradeIdea.thesis: Buy the macro-driven pullback in an AI infrastructure winner. COHR pulled back -21% from its $299 high purely on geopolitical risk-off and profit-taking — no fundamental deterioration. The NVIDIA $2B partnership provides multi-year revenue visibility, and the Bain Capital overhang has been removed. The RSI reset to 48.66 gives room for the next leg up, and max pain at $257.50 creates near-term magnetic pull higher into OpEx.
